title: [Full Workshop] How to add secure code interpreting in your AI app: Vasek Mlejnsky
talk_summary: A workshop by the co-founder of e2b building a Claude-powered code-interpreter app: LLM emits Python via tool-calling, code runs in a Firecracker microVM sandbox, results (stdout, errors, base64 charts) stream back to the frontend. The transferable content is the sandbox architecture (Firecracker microVMs, per-session sandboxes with metadata-based reconnect, Dockerfile-defined environments, VM snapshots) rather than the app-building tutorial.

takeaways.technique: Firecracker microVMs instead of containers for untrusted agent code
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent session gets a full Firecracker microVM (not a container), wrapped in the Jailer to strip dangerous syscalls; escape attempts cause the VM to restart. Boot is ~900ms, targeting ~400ms.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the sandbox is a regular VM it's not a it's not a container ... the reason for that is that we are using something called firecracker

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of creating a fresh sandbox per request (losing context), they list running sandboxes, match on a user-ID stored in sandbox metadata, and reconnect to the existing one; create only if absent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we first check if the sandbox exists for given user ID ... if it exists we connect to the sendbox if it doesn't exist we create a new sandbox

takeaways.what_they_do: Custom environments are declared as an Ubuntu-based Dockerfile (pip/npm installs, env vars, files); they convert the container filesystem into a Firecracker rootfs. Same boot time as prebuilt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you would just give uh give us uh your Docker file and inside a drer file you would have something like pip install whatever you want
takeaways.numbers: custom sandbox starts in same ~900ms as prebuilt

takeaways.technique: VM snapshots for deterministic rollback / tree search
takeaways.what_they_do: Firecracker can snapshot full VM state (memory + filesystem) in ~80ms, letting agents branch and return to a known-good state — proposed as a way to add determinism to non-deterministic agent exploration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can very easily make a snapshot of the whole VM at its current state not only file system uh but also memory

takeaways.technique: Structured execution result object fed back to the model
takeaways.what_they_do: The tool returns a structured object with stdout, stderr, parsed runtime errors with traceback, and rich cell results (PNG/PDF/HTML/JSON), so the LLM can read errors and self-correct.
takeaways.evidence_quote: any runtime errors that are nicely pared uh with uh uh Trace bag that you can feed back into LM so to fix itself

takeaways.technique: Ephemeral sandboxes with no data retention
takeaways.what_they_do: When a sandbox is killed everything is destroyed; only operation metadata is logged, not file contents; persistence is opt-in via mounted cloud storage (S3/FUSE).
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you start a Sandbox um and you kill the sandbox at some point or it just closes by itself uh everything is destroyed
